messages:
maria: FYI Acme support case — they see sudden p99 spikes (~1200ms) and intermittent 502s starting ~10:15 UTC. They say requests are supposed to stay in us-east-1 but traces show hops to eu-west-1. :rotating_light:
support_ek: Thanks, can you paste a couple request IDs and a repro curl? also any CDN / client geo headers they send? :eyes:
maria: Request IDs: req_20260315_54a9, req_20260315_54aa. Customer uses X-Region: us-east-1 header. Example they ran:
```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "X-Region: us-east-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'```
tracebot: ran a quick trace for req_20260315_54a9:
```
trace req_20260315_54a9
-> edge-us-east-1 (accept)
-> auth-proxy-us-east-1 (401 KMS validate timeout)
-> routing-fallback (apply policy: route-to-compatible)
-> edge-eu-west-1 (serve)
latency: total 1.22s (auth wait 680ms)
```
owen: 401 KMS validate timeout at auth-proxy is the smoking gun. If the auth step fails we apply fallback routing which picks a different region’s edge — that explains cross-region hop + p99. Can we share the auth-proxy logs for those req ids?
raj: pulled logs from auth-proxy for the two reqs:
```
1769002468 req_20260315_54a9 INFO auth start hdrs:{X-Region:us-east-1}
1769002468 req_20260315_54a9 WARN kms-validate timeout after 600ms
1769002468 req_20260315_54a9 INFO fallback triggered -> route-to-compatible
1769002491 req_20260315_54aa INFO auth start hdrs:{X-Region:us-east-1}
1769002491 req_20260315_54aa WARN kms-validate transient error code=502 backend-unreach
1769002491 req_20260315_54aa INFO fallback triggered -> route-to-compatible
```
raj: Looks like KMS validation to the regional KMS endpoint had increased latency / transient 502s. When we fail auth we don't block; policy opts for best-effort route which picks eu-west-1.
devops-bot: alert fired: cross-region-egress spike from us-east-1 -> eu-west-1, p99 increase 18% starting 10:12 UTC. Alert link: https://alerts.redwood.ai/incident/INC-2026-0315-12
support_ek: short-term mitigation: advise customer to set strict-region-binding header (X-Region-Bind: strict) which will return 429/403 instead of routing elsewhere so at least they see auth failure rather than elevated latency. Also ask them to retry with a cached token or increase KMS timeout to reduce transient failures.
maria: sent that to Acme; they prefer availability over erroring. Is there a platform-side change we can do to avoid big latency delta when KMS hiccups?
owen: long-term we should avoid global fallback on auth failures — change fallback policy to prefer same-region retry with backoff before route-to-different-region. Also add a short-lived KMS replica / warm standby in nearby AZs to reduce validate latency.
raj: I can add a quick rule: if KMS validate times out < 1s, do 1 retry to the same-region KMS before fallback. I'll open a PR and can toggle in canary for us-east-1.
maria: please also expose a per-tenant override so premium customers can opt-in to strict-region-binding.
owen: agree. I'll make the policy configurable and add a metric for "fallback-due-to-auth" so we can track.
tracebot: re-run after raj's proposed retry (dry run):
```
req_20260315_54a9 dry-run-retry -> kms-validate retry1 success (240ms)
path: edge-us-east-1 -> auth-proxy-us-east-1 -> edge-us-east-1
latency: total 420ms
```
support_ek: great sign. Action items: raj PR for retry logic (ETA 3h), owen policy config (ETA EOD), support to update KB and advise Acme to set X-Region-Bind if they want strict. I'll keep ticket open until we see no more cross-region serves. :white_check_mark:
maria: thanks all — forwarding summary to Acme now. Closing here after monitoring window (30m).
